doc.title: Jerry Dodgion interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 9, 1996

title: Thad bringing out the best; the 'Vanguard Conservatory'
summary: He praises Thad, and jokes with orchestra colleagues that he attended the Vanguard Conservatory for twelve years.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: Maybe just phonetically it was good. I don’t think there was any deep spiritual attachment. But Thad was marvelous. He just brought the best out of everyone. I mean anyone who came into the band to play, even just for a few days or a day, they would walk away with, “How did I do that? I can’t do that, I can’t play that.” Because he would do that. He just brought the best out of everyone. I mean the humanity level was great. The music was great. It was just the greatest experience imaginable. So when I started doing dates with, you know you’d do an orchestra date or something, the guy next to you went to Juilliard and he’s talking about Juilliard. And the guy on this side, he went to Curtis you know, and they’re talking about their conservatories and they look at me like I’m supposed to say something. So I say, “Well I went to the Vanguard Conservatory,” I says, “I’m still there.” I said, “At this time I was at the Conservatory for twelve years.“ And they look very, you know, quizzical looks. Never heard of that one you know. It was a lot of fun though.
